title: The Resilience Fund can be used when Sky itself is the target, but the protocol for that case does not yet exist
content:
A.2.9.1.1.1 scopes the fund to actions "against Sky **or** active participants," yet the machinery in A.2.9.1.1.1.3 and .1.4 is built entirely around individual Beneficiaries — proof of eligibility via a personal Ethereum address, role-based beneficiary categories, coverage that expires after a beneficiary's role ends. None of it fits Sky as respondent.

A.2.9.1.1.1.1.2 acknowledges the gap and bridges it provisionally: Sky-related legal defense expenses "may be temporarily financed using the resources of the Resilience Fund," but "a separate Claim Protocol and Standard Operational Protocol must be developed to govern cases where Sky is the target." The annotation at A.2.9.1.1.1.1.2.0.3.1 confirms the status plainly — "[t]hese separate procedures have not yet been defined," to be placed in A.2.9.1.1.4 once ratified, with the Resilience Technical Committee required to assist.

The exposure is asymmetric with the fund's own risk profile. An action against Sky is the scenario most likely to consume the entire 5,000,000 USDS annual budget and to demand immediate spending, and it is the one case with no eligibility test, no exclusion list, and no approval path — only permission to spend.

The honest reading is that the fund's individual-contributor programme is mature and its institutional-defense programme is a placeholder holding a spending authorization. Anyone assessing Sky's legal preparedness should not read the fund's existence as coverage for Sky itself.
description: Transition funding permits temporary financing of Sky-related legal defense while requiring a separate Claim Protocol that the annotation confirms is still undefined and awaits Committee input.
